idiom_name: @dataclass(kw_only=True) with per-field defaults, or plain keyword arguments
implementation_notes: The builder exists in Java to simulate named optional parameters; Python has them, so the main case is solved by the language: keyword arguments let a caller name what matters and omit the rest, and @dataclass (or attrs/pydantic) generates that constructor with defaults, field(default_factory=...) and __post_init__ as the validation hook, while dataclasses.replace(obj, **changes) covers the "same object, one field changed" case a builder's reuse provided. Write the fluent builder only when the object is assembled from genuinely conditional steps or when one sequence must produce different representations.
code_sketch:
@dataclass(kw_only=True, frozen=True)
class House:
    walls: str
    roof: str
    floors: int = 1
    windows: int = 4
    has_garage: bool = False

h = House(walls="brick", roof="tile", has_garage=True)
pitfalls: Keyword arguments give no ordering or completeness guarantee beyond required fields: rules spanning fields need __post_init__ (with object.__setattr__ under frozen=True) or a validating factory.
A frozen=True dataclass still shares a mutable default (list or dict) between instances unless the default comes from field(default_factory=...).
If the constructor accepts **kwargs, unknown keys are silently accepted; keyword-only parameters make a typo raise TypeError instead.

variants.name: Immutable fluent builder (step-wise query construction)
variants.idiom_name: SQLAlchemy Core select().where(...).order_by(...): every step returns a new construct
variants.implementation_notes: Where construction really is incremental, Python libraries use an immutable builder: each method returns a new object carrying the added clause instead of mutating shared state - SQLAlchemy 2.0 documents Select as immutable, so where(), order_by() and limit() produce fresh constructs that can be stored, branched and reused safely, and there is no separate terminal build() because the accumulated object is the product. That is the functional form of the pattern: the builder is a value and the partial result is useful on its own.
variants.code_sketch:
base = select(User).where(User.active.is_(True))    # reusable template
recent = base.where(User.created_at > cutoff)       # returns a new Select
page = recent.order_by(User.name).limit(20)
rows = session.execute(page).scalars().all()
pitfalls: Copy-on-step allocates: each step clones the construct's current state, so branching thousands of times in a hot loop costs accordingly.
With no terminal validation point there is no single place to reject an invalid combination; the database or the consumer becomes the first validator.
